proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\ell_{m,\delta}^-\) and \(\ell_{m,\delta}^+\) for the regularized losses in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}terminal\text{-}envelopes}\).  Directly from the formulas for \(f_\delta^-\) and \(f_\delta^+\), for every \(a\in\mathbb R\),
\[
f_\delta^-(a)\leq\mathbf 1\{a<0\}\leq f_\delta^+(a).
\tag{1}
\]
Multiplying (1) by the nonnegative quantities \(w_j\mathbf 1\{h_j^m>0\}\), summing over \(j\), and using \(\sum_jw_j=1\), gives
\[
0\leq\ell_{m,\delta}^-\leq\ell_m\leq
\ell_{m,\delta}^+\leq1.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(c_{m,\delta}^\pm\) denotes the corresponding untruncated oracle value, monotonicity of expectation and then of the infimum gives
\[
B_\delta^-(\lambda)\leq B(\lambda)\leq B_\delta^+(\lambda),
\qquad
c_{m,\delta}^-\leq c_m\leq c_{m,\delta}^+.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus regularization bounds the observed-law design functionals and does not redefine the target \(V\).

\emph{Continuity on retained states.}
Put \(c_H=H+H^2/2\), \(s_k=x_k-q_k/2\), and
\[
e_I(x,q)=|I|^{-1}\sum_{k\in I}\exp(s_k).
\]
Along any line segment, \(f_\delta^\pm\circ a_j\) is absolutely continuous.  At almost every point where its derivative is nonzero, an active intersection \(I\ni j\) obeys
\[
19<20-\delta\leq e_I(x,q)\leq20+\delta<21.
\tag{4}
\]
At such a point,
\[
\sum_{k\in I}\left|\frac{\partial e_I}{\partial x_k}\right|
=e_I<21,
\qquad
\sum_{k\in I}\left|\frac{\partial e_I}{\partial q_k}\right|
=\frac12e_I<\frac{21}{2}.
\tag{5}
\]
The envelope slope is at most \(1/\delta\).  Integrating (5) along the segment, using that the minimum of finitely many Lipschitz functions has the maximum of their Lipschitz constants, and summing weights bounded by one yields
\[
|\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm(x,q)-\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm(x',q')|
\leq\frac{32}{\delta}\|(x,q)-(x',q')\|_\infty .
\tag{6}
\]
This calculation uses neither division by \(q_j\) nor a positive lower bound on an allocation clock.

For the likelihood ratio in the frozen core,
\[
d\log Z_m
=\sum_jh_j^m\,dx_j-\frac12\sum_j(h_j^m)^2\,dq_j.
\tag{7}
\]
Since \(|h_j^m|\leq H\), a state displacement of sup norm at most \(d\) gives
\[
|\log Z_m-\log Z_m'|\leq Kc_Hd.
\tag{8}
\]
For a fixed prior, differentiation of
\(b_m^\lambda=\lambda_mZ_m/\sum_r\lambda_rZ_r\) gives
\[
db_m^\lambda=b_m^\lambda\left(d\log Z_m-
\sum_rb_r^\lambda\,d\log Z_r\right),
\]
and hence
\[
\sum_m|db_m^\lambda|\leq2Kc_Hd.
\tag{9}
\]
The formula is still valid when some \(\lambda_m=0\), because the corresponding posterior coordinate is identically zero.  It follows from (6) and (9) that the normalized posterior payoff
\(g=\sum_mb_m^\lambda\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm\) has modulus
\[
\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+2Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]

Fix a score guard and let
\[
C_G=\max_{\text{guard box}}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m,
\qquad
S=\frac{\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m}{C_G}.
\tag{11}
\]
The guard contains \((x,q)=(0,0)\), where every \(Z_m\) equals one, so
\[
C_G\geq\sum_m\lambda_m=1.
\tag{12}
\]
On a segment inside the guard, \(0\leq S\leq1\), and the logarithmic derivative of \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\) is the posterior-weighted average of the logarithmic derivatives in (7).  Equations (8) and (12) therefore imply
\[
|S-S'|\leq Kc_Hd.
\tag{13}
\]
Because \(0\leq g,g',S,S'\leq1\),
\[
|Sg-S'g'|\leq |g-g'|+|S-S'|.
\]
Combining this inequality with (10) and (13) proves the corrected retained-state modulus
\[
\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+3Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\tag{14}
\]
The outer minimum uses the range bound and is required whenever the linear expression is at least one.

Couple two diffusions started at two retained states at the same time by using the same future Brownian motions and by feeding the second control the first translated state history.  The controls then agree, and the terminal score--clock displacement equals the initial displacement.  Applying (6), (10), and (14), and taking infima in both directions, propagates \(\Omega_\delta\) for normalized posterior values and \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\) for scaled unnormalized values so long as both coupled paths remain viable.  The construction below treats a nonviable successor by exact killing, so continuity is invoked only on retained cells.  This argument remains valid on zero-allocation faces.

\emph{Likelihood identity and mesh-exit truncation.}
Under the zero-drift reference law, bounded predictability and successive Gaussian conditioning show for every simple predictable control that
\[
Z_m(X(t),Q(t))
=\exp\!\left\{\sum_jh_j^mX_j(t)
-\frac12\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_j(t)\right\}
\tag{15}
\]
is a mean-one likelihood process.  General progressively measurable controls follow by approximation in stochastic-integral norm, because
\(\sum_j\int_0^1(h_j^m)^2u_j(t)\,dt\leq H^2\).
Consequently, for every bounded terminal functional \(R\),
\[
\mathbb E_m^u[R]=\mathbb E_0^u[Z_m(X(1),Q(1))R].
\tag{16}
\]

For a partition \(\Pi=\{0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=1\}\), define
\[
\tau_{G,\Pi}
=\min\{t_l\in\Pi:\max_j|X_j(t_l)|\geq G\},
\tag{17}
\]
with the minimum of the empty set equal to infinity, and define
\[
L_{m,G,\Pi,\delta}^{\pm}(u)
=\mathbb E_m^u\!\left[
\ell_{m,\delta}^{\pm}(X(1),Q(1))
\mathbf 1\{\tau_{G,\Pi}>1\}\right].
\tag{18}
\]
The same notation without \(\delta,\pm\) denotes the truncated original loss.  In a backward recursion, (18) is represented by sending the first transition with \(\max_j|X_j|\geq G\) to an absorbing cemetery state whose value is exactly zero.  Thus a path that later reenters cannot regain value.

At a retained terminal state, the prior-weighted reference datum divided by \(C_G\) equals
\[
C_G^{-1}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm=Sg\in[0,1].
\tag{19}
\]
At a killed state it is zero.  Hence the zero extension of the scaled truncated datum is globally \([0,1]\)-valued.  This is the bounded datum used in interpolation and Gaussian quadrature; no bound on the untruncated likelihood ratio outside the guard is asserted.

Under scenario \(m\),
\[
X_j(t)=h_j^mQ_j(t)+M_j(t),\qquad
M_j(t)=\int_0^t\sqrt{u_j(s)}\,dW_j(s),\qquad 0\leq Q_j(t)\leq1.
\tag{20}
\]
Successive conditioning for simple controls and stochastic-integral approximation for general controls show that
\(\exp\{\theta M_j(t)-\theta^2Q_j(t)/2\}\) is a mean-one nonnegative martingale.  Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}howard\text{-}linear\text{-}boundary}\) to \(M_j\) and \(-M_j\), take \(\theta=G-H>0\), and use \(Q_j(t)\leq1\).  A union bound over \(j\) gives
\[
\sup_{m,u}\Pr_m^u\!\left\{\max_j\sup_{t\leq1}|X_j(t)|\geq G\right\}
\leq p_G:=2K\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(G-H)^2}{2}\right\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Since \(\{\tau_{G,\Pi}\leq1\}\) is contained in the event in (21), (2) implies, for every policy and for the original or either regularized loss,
\[
0\leq L_m(u)-L_{m,G,\Pi}(u)
\leq\Pr_m^u(\tau_{G,\Pi}\leq1)\leq p_G.
\tag{22}
\]
Taking the prior-weighted sum and then infima over \(u\), or taking the scenario infimum, yields
\[
B_{G,\Pi}\leq B\leq B_{G,\Pi}+p_G,\qquad
c_{m,G,\Pi}\leq c_m\leq c_{m,G,\Pi}+p_G.
\tag{23}
\]
In particular,
\[
B_{G,\Pi}-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,G,\Pi}-p_G
\leq B-\sum_m\lambda_mc_m
\leq B_{G,\Pi}-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,G,\Pi}+p_G.
\tag{24}
\]
This proves that guard truncation enlarges each side of a Bayes-regret enclosure by \(p_G\), and therefore contributes at most \(2p_G\) to its width.

Equation (16) also identifies the omitted prior mixture under the reference law:
\[
\mathbb E_0^u\!\left[
\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_m\mathbf 1\{\tau_{G,\Pi}\leq1\}\right]
=\sum_m\lambda_m
\mathbb E_m^u[\ell_m\mathbf 1\{\tau_{G,\Pi}\leq1\}]
\leq p_G.
\tag{25}
\]
Before undoing the scale, (25) contributes at most \(p_G/C_G\); after multiplication by \(C_G\), it contributes \(p_G\).  Thus the guard term is controlled under the observed scenario laws and is not replaced by a reference Gaussian quadrature-tail probability.

\emph{Validated killed recursion.}
Suppose vertices \(v\) of a viable state cell carry intervals enclosing a scaled continuation function \(F\), and \(y\) has multilinear barycentric weights \(\beta_v\).  If the cell has diameter \(d\), (14) gives
\[
\left|F(y)-\sum_v\beta_vF(v)\right|
\leq\sum_v\beta_v\widetilde\Omega_\delta(\|y-v\|_\infty)
\leq\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d).
\tag{26}
\]
For a time increment \(a>0\), constant allocation \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\), and standard Gaussian vector \(z\), the reference transition is
\[
(x,q)\longmapsto
\bigl(x+(av)^{1/2}\mathbin\odot z,\ q+av\bigr).
\tag{27}
\]
For every retained Gaussian cell, interval arithmetic encloses the entire image of (27).  A successor outside the guard is assigned zero exactly; an inside successor is evaluated with (26).  The products of nonnegative continuation and outward-rounded probability intervals, summed outward, enclose the retained-cell expectation.

The complement of the truncated standardized-Gaussian quadrature box may be multiplied by \([0,1]\), but only because (19) and absorbing killing make the scaled continuation globally \([0,1]\)-valued.  This Gaussian integration tail is a distinct ledger item from (25).  Coupling allocations \(v,v'\) with the same \(z\), and using
\((\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\leq|p-q|\), bounds the control-net error by
\[
\mathbb E\,\widetilde\Omega_\delta\!\left(
a\|v-v'\|_1+
\sqrt{a\|v-v'\|_1}\,\|z\|_2\right).
\tag{28}
\]
Bounded convergence makes (28) tend uniformly to zero with the control-net radius.  Minimizing lower endpoints after subtracting this error and upper endpoints after adding it encloses the Bellman infimum over the full simplex.  Backward induction using (26)--(28) validates the killed Bayes recursion.  The same argument validates every killed fixed-policy recursion and every killed point-mass-oracle recursion.

Effective rational outward bounds for retained Gaussian-cell probabilities follow from rational Taylor bounds for \(\exp(-z^2/2)\) on compact intervals.  Omitted Gaussian mass is enclosed using the global range \([0,1]\).  All these operations are finite rational interval operations for a fixed candidate.

\emph{Passage from the finite recursion to continuous control.}
Let \(P_a^v\) denote the Gaussian operator in (27), before absorption at a nonviable successor, and let
\[
\mathcal L^v\phi
=\frac12\sum_jv_j\partial_{x_jx_j}\phi+
\sum_jv_j\partial_{q_j}\phi.
\tag{29}
\]
On retained states the exact regularized recursion satisfies
\[
J_l=\min_{v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)}P_{a_l}^vJ_{l+1},
\qquad
J_l\leq P_{a_l}^vJ_{l+1}\quad\text{for every }v,
\tag{30}
\]
where \(a_l=t_{l+1}-t_l\) and the operator assigns zero at an exterior successor.

Convolve the scaled multilinear lower interpolants on the inner score box with a rational compactly supported \(C^3\) tensor mollifier of radius \(\kappa\), chosen with support inside the guard.  Its terminal and intermediate errors are bounded using \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(\kappa)\).  If the certified one-layer error is \(\xi_l\), subtracting \(\sum_{s\geq l}\xi_s\) restores the second inequality in (30) for the smoothed lower interpolants.  Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives
\[
P_a^v\phi-\phi-a\mathcal L^v\phi=\mathcal R_a^v(\phi).
\tag{31}
\]
Derivative intervals for the mollified interpolant and truncated Gaussian moments give outward rational bounds for \(\mathcal R_a^v\).  For fixed \(\kappa\), the score remainder is bounded by a computable multiple of \(a^{3/2}\kappa^{-3}\), the clock remainder by a computable multiple of \(a^2\kappa^{-2}\), and the interpolation contribution by the \(\xi_l\) computed from (14).  The enumerated refinements include
\[
\max_la_l\downarrow0,\quad
\sum_l\xi_l\downarrow0,\quad
\max_l\frac{\xi_l}{a_l}\downarrow0,\quad
\kappa\downarrow0,\quad
\max_la_l^{1/2}\kappa^{-3}\downarrow0.
\tag{32}
\]
Such a diagonal refinement exists because
\(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)\to0\) for each fixed \(\delta>0\).

Linear interpolation in time produces computable \(e_T\geq0\) and \(e_B(t)\geq0\) such that, on the retained domain,
\[
\phi^-(1,\cdot)\leq
C_G^{-1}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm,\qquad
\phi^-\leq0\ \text{on the absorbing boundary},
\]
\[
\partial_t\phi^-+\mathcal L^v\phi^-\geq-e_B(t)
\quad\text{for every }v\in\Delta(\mathcal J),
\qquad
e_T+\int_0^1e_B(t)\,dt\longrightarrow0.
\tag{33}
\]
For simple predictable controls killed at the mesh boundary, successive conditional Gaussian integrations and (31) telescope.  Since
\(\mathcal L^u=\sum_ju_j\mathcal L^{e_j}\), their scaled killed risk is at least
\[
\phi^-(0,0,0)-\int_0^1e_B(t)\,dt.
\tag{34}
\]
All quantities are bounded on the retained domain, so stochastic-integral approximation extends (34) to every progressively measurable control.  This verifies the lower endpoint directly and does not assume generalized-terminal comparison or global HJB uniqueness.

For the upper endpoint, the grid recursion selects a predictable piecewise-constant control and the independent killed fixed-policy recursion encloses its risk.  Predictable simple simplex-valued processes \(v^{(N)}\) approximate every \(u\in\mathcal U\) with
\[
\mathbb E\int_0^1\|u(t)-v^{(N)}(t)\|_1\,dt\longrightarrow0.
\tag{35}
\]
The It\^o isometry and the square-root inequality imply
\[
\mathbb E\|Q^u(1)-Q^{v^{(N)}}(1)\|_1\longrightarrow0,
\]
\[
\sum_j\mathbb E\left|
\int_0^1(\sqrt{u_j(t)}-\sqrt{v_j^{(N)}(t)})\,dW_j(t)
\right|^2\longrightarrow0.
\tag{36}
\]
The drift displacement is at most \(H\) times the clock displacement.  Equations (6) and (36) yield convergence of every untruncated regularized scenario risk, uniformly over the finite scenario set.  The guard comparison (22), uniformly bounded by \(p_G\), then yields convergence for the killed risks as \(G\to\infty\).  Approximating the finitely many simple action values by rational control-net points using (28) proves convergence of lower and upper killed Bellman endpoints to the same regularized control value.  Coordinates with \(v_j=0\) remain fixed in (27) and have zero coefficient in (29), so no forced exploration is used.

\emph{Regularization, minimax assembly, and termination.}
Define
\[
\mathcal G(\lambda)=B(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_m
=\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_m\lambda_mr_m(u).
\tag{37}
\]
Since \(0\leq r_m(u)\leq1\),
\[
|\mathcal G(\lambda)-\mathcal G(\lambda')|
\leq\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_1.
\tag{38}
\]
The rational simplex net with denominator \(D\) contains every point mass and has \(\ell_1\)-covering radius at most \(2(M-1)/D\).  The already established Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}least\text{-}favorable\text{-}saddle}\) gives
\[
V=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\mathcal G(\lambda).
\tag{39}
\]
For every prior-net point, (3) gives
\[
B_\delta^-(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,\delta}^+
\leq\mathcal G(\lambda)\leq
B_\delta^+(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,\delta}^-.
\tag{40}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\text{-}terminal\text{-}comparison}\) bounds the width in (40) by
\[
\bigl(B_\delta^+-B_\delta^-\bigr)
+\sum_m\lambda_m(c_{m,\delta}^+-c_{m,\delta}^-)
\leq2\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\eta),
\tag{41}
\]
and \(\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\sqrt\delta)\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).  Applying (24) separately to the lower and upper regularized values adds \(p_G\) to each endpoint and at most \(2p_G\) to the gap; it does not merge the guard and terminal-envelope ledger entries.  Equations (38)--(41), the point-mass recursions, and the prior-net covering radius give certified dual bounds including the oracle offsets.

If an independently evaluated finite policy mixture has truncated upper scenario-risk endpoints \(L_{m,G,\Pi}^+\) and the point-mass recursion gives lower truncated-oracle endpoints \(c_{m,G,\Pi}^-\), then (23) implies
\[
r_m(u)\leq L_{m,G,\Pi}^+(u)+p_G-c_{m,G,\Pi}^-,
\qquad
V\leq\max_m\{L_{m,G,\Pi}^+(u)+p_G-c_{m,G,\Pi}^-\}.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the primal endpoint is valid independently of the optimization recursion that selected the mixture.

For fixed \(\delta\) and \(G\), equations (14), (26)--(36), Gaussian-cell refinement, quadrature-tail refinement, mollification, and outward-rounding refinement make every numerical term tend to zero.  Next take \(G\uparrow\infty\), so \(p_G\downarrow0\) by (21), and then take \(\eta=\sqrt\delta\) and \(\delta\downarrow0\), so (41) tends to zero.  Finally refine the prior net, using (38).  Therefore the candidate lower endpoints approach \(V\) from below.

For upper endpoints, take the finite \(\epsilon\)-saddle mixture of Markov Bayes responses supplied by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}least\text{-}favorable\text{-}saddle}\).  A prior-net point within radius \(r_\lambda\) of its least-favorable prior makes each component \(2r_\lambda\)-Bayes, because both a fixed policy's Bayes risk and the Bayes value are \(1\)-Lipschitz in the prior.  Equations (35)--(36) approximate the finitely many components by enumerated rational-grid policies; sufficiently fine enumeration retains them.  Their mixture is feasible for the finite rational scenario-risk linear program.  Equations (21), (41), and the independent bound (42) make its certified upper endpoint at most \(V+\epsilon+o(1)\).  Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves convergence of cumulative primal upper endpoints down to \(V\).

Every candidate computation is finite.  Rational Taylor enclosures evaluate Gaussian cell probabilities and the elementary functions on bounded boxes; finite rational linear programs solve the primal and dual net problems.  The deterministic enumeration contains \(\delta\downarrow0\), \(\eta=\sqrt\delta\), \(G\uparrow\infty\), and all refinements in (32).  Because \(p_G\to0\), the Gaussian quadrature tail tends to zero independently, and all scaled-datum continuity terms use (14), the complete candidate-specific ledger tends to zero.  Hence for every \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}>0\) a finite candidate has certified gap at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), so enumeration reaches such a candidate and terminates.  Cumulative maxima of valid lower endpoints are nondecreasing; cumulative minima of independently validated upper endpoints are nonincreasing.  At termination,
\[
\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
\overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}
\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}},
\tag{43}
\]
and (42) certifies the returned mixture \(u\) by
\[
\max_{1\leq m\leq M}r_m(u)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}.
\tag{44}
\]

Finally, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}boundary\text{-}stable\text{-}frontier}\) transfers the returned mixture's scenario-risk vector to predictable finite-horizon policies and gives \(c_{n,m}\to c_m\).  Since \(M\) is finite,
\[
\max_mr_{n,m}(\pi_n)
=\max_mr_m(u)+o(1)
\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1).
\tag{45}
\]
The transfer invokes the theorem's repaired reference-law Markovization and continuous-kernel block construction; it does not require the allocation clocks to encode ordered histories.  Only the declared finite scenario list and \(|h_j^m|\leq H\) enter the guard argument, so no null-boundary closure or forced-exploration premise is added.  The proof establishes termination and qualitative certified convergence, but no closed-form mesh size, arithmetic complexity bound, convergence rate, or interval-certified numerical value.

proposed.name: finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm
proposed.construction:
Given \(\mathfrak E\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate deterministically all finite binary-rational candidates consisting of lower and upper terminal-envelope widths \(\delta\), small-information cutoffs \(\eta\), an inner score box and a strictly larger guard box, time and allocation-clock meshes, a finite rational control net in the allocation simplex, a finite rational prior net in \(\Delta_M\) containing every point mass, a rational near-Bayes retention tolerance, a partition of a truncated standardized Gaussian box into rational cells, and an outward-rounding precision.  Every time partition \(\Pi=\{0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=1\}\) and score guard \(G>H\) define the mesh-detected exit time
\[
\tau_{G,\Pi}=\min\{t_l\in\Pi:\max_{j\in\mathcal J}|X_j(t_l)|\geq G\},
\]
with \(\tau_{G,\Pi}=\infty\) when the set is empty.  The regularized terminal quantities computed on this candidate are
\[
\ell_{m,\delta}^{\pm}(X(1),Q(1))
\mathbf 1\{\tau_{G,\Pi}>1\}.
\]
Exterior states are sent to an absorbing cemetery state of value zero: every transition whose successor has \(\max_j|X_j|\geq G\) receives continuation value exactly zero, and a killed path remains at zero.  This is mesh-exit truncation, not continuous first-exit monitoring.  Put
\[
p_G=2K\exp\{-(G-H)^2/2\}.
\]
The observed-law guard ledger uses
\[
0\leq L_m(u)-L_{m,G,\Pi}(u)\leq p_G,
\quad
B_{G,\Pi}\leq B\leq B_{G,\Pi}+p_G,
\quad
c_{m,G,\Pi}\leq c_m\leq c_{m,G,\Pi}+p_G,
\]
with the same inequalities for each regularized lower or upper loss.  Consequently the certified Bayes-regret endpoints are enlarged by \(p_G\) on each side, the total certified gap is charged by at most \(2p_G\), and an independently evaluated policy is bounded by
\[
r_m(u)\leq L_{m,G,\Pi}^{+}(u)+p_G-c_{m,G,\Pi}^{-}.
\]

Put \(c_H=H+H^2/2\).  For the normalized posterior terminal payoff use
\[
\Omega_\delta(d)=\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+2Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\]
For each prior \(\lambda\), let \(C_G\) be the computable maximum of \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\) on the guard box, write \(S=(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m)/C_G\), and scale the lower and upper regularized versions of \(F_\lambda\) by \(C_G^{-1}\).  The guard contains the origin, so \(C_G\geq1\).  On retained states \(0\leq S\leq1\), while the absorbing zero extension makes the scaled truncated datum globally \([0,1]\)-valued.  For that scaled unnormalized datum \(Sg\), use throughout
\[
\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+3Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\]
Propagate the scaled killed values backward on the viable state cells and undo the scale at the initial state.  At a state cell of diameter \(d\), the interval interpolant is the barycentric sum of the vertex intervals enlarged by \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)\).  Use this same scaled-datum modulus in state and control-net estimates whenever terminal continuity is invoked, in mollification error, in Bellman residual and finite-horizon accumulation, in every killed fixed-policy and point-mass-oracle recursion, and in the corresponding entries of the actual certificate ledger; when its linear expression is at least one, use the range bound one.

For every control-net point, scenario, and retained Gaussian cell, outward-round the cell probability, enclose the entire image of that cell under the score-clock transition, multiply the probability interval by the resulting continuation interval, and sum outward.  A retained-cell transition outside the guard receives exactly zero.  Only omitted mass from the separately truncated standardized-Gaussian quadrature is multiplied by \([0,1]\), which is valid because the killed scaled continuation has the global range \([0,1]\).  Never use that quadrature-tail bound for the omitted untruncated likelihood-weighted guard contribution: the latter is charged by the observed-law bound \(p_G\), or by \(p_G/C_G\) before undoing the reference-law scale.  A rational compactly supported mollification of the multilinear interpolants is checked cell by cell against the killed reference-law Bellman operators; Taylor's formula with integral remainder supplies a certified time-discretization and control residual, and the same recursion supplies its finite-horizon accumulated bound.  Run the identical killed validated recursion at every point-mass prior to enclose the regularized versions of \(c_m\).  Retain every enumerated grid policy certified to be near-Bayes at some prior-net point, solve outward-rounded rational primal and dual scenario-risk linear programs over those columns, and independently re-evaluate the selected finite policy mixture by a killed fixed-policy interval recursion.  Extend the dual search from the prior net using the \(\ell_1\)-Lipschitz bound for the Bayes-regret functional.

Form a ledger from the actual certified terminal-regularization, observed-law guard-exit, time-discretization, scaled-datum interpolation and control-mesh, Gaussian-cell, Gaussian-quadrature-tail, mollification and Bellman-residual accumulation, oracle and linear-program, recovered-policy, prior-net, and rounding contributions, with every scaled-datum continuity contribution recomputed from \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\).  Apply the guard charge to the Bayes, fixed-policy, and point-mass-oracle endpoints as displayed above and charge at most \(2p_G\) to an affected certified gap, keeping terminal-envelope terms separate.  Replace each lower endpoint by the maximum and each upper endpoint by the minimum over all candidates examined so far.  Accept the first candidate for which the sum of the applicable certified ledger bounds is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\); call the resulting cumulative endpoints \(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\) and \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former exterior interval was invalid for the untruncated likelihood-weighted reference payoff.  The corrected construction kills paths at mesh-detected guard exit, assigns exterior successors exactly zero, and charges the omitted contribution under each observed scenario law by the uniform guard probability.

prose_updates.tldr: For any declared finite bounded list of local causal-effect scenarios, the fixed arithmetic-mean closed e-test admits an adaptive subgroup-recruitment minimax-regret frontier. Exact Gaussian grid embedding and a quantitative terminal-envelope comparison transfer its discontinuous rejection risk, including zero-allocation faces, to and from the controlled score diffusion. Finite-scenario convex duality yields an attained least-favorable prior and posterior-state Markov response. A deterministic nested interval Bellman search uses absorbing zero-exterior mesh truncation, an observed-law guard-exit charge, and independent recovered-policy evaluation to supply convergent certified bounds. This object is complementary to the repository's unrestricted finite-population binary-contrast design-and-estimation frontier.

project_justification.fill: The project proves exact Gaussian grid embedding, quantitative boundary-stable transfer for the discontinuous rejection surfaces, uniform Bayes and oracle convergence, minimax-regret convergence, and predictable finite-policy attainment. For policy recovery it Markovizes a selected finite rule at the score--clock state under the zero-drift reference law, preserves every declared scenario terminal risk by terminal likelihood tilting, regularizes the finitely many action kernels simultaneously, and then applies a continuous-kernel block construction. It also proves termination of a deterministic nested interval-Bellman search. That search kills paths at mesh-detected guard exit, assigns exterior continuations exactly zero, charges the omitted likelihood-weighted contribution through a uniform observed-law exit bound, keeps Gaussian quadrature tails separate, and independently re-evaluates the returned policy mixture.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The common-drift translation and initial-state envelope squeeze do not prove comparison or uniqueness at every off-origin viable boundary state. The certificate therefore uses direct finite-horizon Bellman enclosure and stopped-process verification for continuous terminal envelopes, not global generalized-terminal HJB uniqueness. Its scaled unnormalized reference datum uses the corrected modulus \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=\min\{1,(32/\delta+3K(H+H^2/2))d\}\) only on retained cells. Exterior successors are absorbed at zero at mesh monitoring times; the omitted untruncated likelihood-weighted contribution is charged under the observed scenario laws by \(p_G=2K\exp\{-(G-H)^2/2\}\), separately from standardized-Gaussian quadrature tails. This is not continuous first-exit monitoring. Termination is qualitative and computable; no closed-form mesh schedule, arithmetic operation count, convergence rate, or interval-certified nontrivial numerical run is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives a reproducible epsilon certificate because every exterior successor is absorbed at zero, the omitted likelihood-weighted guard contribution is charged by a uniform observed-law exit bound, Gaussian quadrature tails are kept distinct, every scaled-datum continuity term is computed from the corrected modulus, and the returned policy mixture is independently re-evaluated.
